page: Vultr vcg-a16-6c-64g-16vram is a dedicated bare metal instance belonging to the Dedicated Metal GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 architecture with 6 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 3 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of a 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 64.0 GB, yielding a memory-to-core density of 10.67 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 350 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yielded scores of 1745.38 and 10619.81 respectively, both falling into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests showed 586.08 GB/sec for small block cached reads, and 76.25 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. While single-threaded bzip3 decompression performed at an average rate of 10.12 GB/sec, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered a weaker result of 30.39 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25 percent. Conversely, the instance demonstrated top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing, achieving 8771.1 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 591.21 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The inclusion of a dedicated 350 GB NVMe SSD provides local storage without requiring external attachments. Given the average database operations score of 2986.48 and redis SET throughput of 10.78 million operations per second, this server is suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks.
